extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their financial reporting / compliance teams (preparers of SEC filings)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and interpretive guidance for disclosing expenditures, capitalized costs, charges, and losses related to severe weather events and other natural conditions (and limited rules for carbon offsets/RECs) under amended Regulation S-X / Article 14. Includes thresholds, denominators, attribution principles, presentation, and related contextual-disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of expenditures expensed and losses from severe weather/other natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose the aggregate amount of expenditures expensed as incurred and losses, excluding recoveries, incurred during the fiscal year as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amounts disclosed should be those already captured in the income statement and measured under U.S. GAAP or IFRS. The disclosure is subject to the one percent disclosure threshold (income-statement denominator) and de minimis exception ($100,000), and recoveries must be separately disclosed as contextual information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of capitalized costs and charges from severe weather/other natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose the aggregate amount of capitalized costs and charges, excluding recoveries, recognized during the fiscal year as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amounts are those recorded on the balance sheet and measured under U.S. GAAP or IFRS. The disclosure is subject to the one percent disclosure threshold (balance-sheet denominator) and de minimis exception ($500,000), and registrants must separately disclose where on the balance sheet such amounts are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution principle for 'as a result of' determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must use a prescribed attribution principle to determine whether a capitalized cost, expenditure expensed, charge, or loss is 'as a result of' a severe weather event or other natural condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attribution principle is intended to simplify determinations by eliminating the need to allocate portions of costs and expenditures, reducing compliance costs. It governs how to identify discrete costs incurred due to severe weather events and other natural conditions rather than forecasting or allocating mitigation/transition motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: One percent quantitative disclosure threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules retain a bright-line one percent disclosure threshold for (1) expenditures expensed and losses (income-statement disclosures) and (2) capitalized costs and charges (balance-sheet disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For income-statement items, disclosure is required if aggregate expenditures expensed and losses equal or exceed one percent of the absolute value of income or loss before income tax expense or benefit for the fiscal year. For balance-sheet items, disclosure is required if aggregate capitalized costs and charges recognized equal or exceed one percent of the absolute value of stockholders' equity or deficit at fiscal year-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominators for the disclosure thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The denominators for the one percent threshold are (1) income or loss before income tax expense or benefit for income-statement disclosures and (2) stockholders' equity or deficit for balance-sheet disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These denominators were chosen because they are well-known, easily calculable from GAAP/IFRS financial statements, promote comparability, and may help registrants estimate denominators in advance to establish internal controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of absolute values in threshold calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure thresholds should be calculated using the absolute values of the relevant denominators, and the absolute value of capitalized costs and charges recognized for the numerator when determining balance-sheet thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute values avoid confusion from debit/credit conventions and ensure the full magnitude of costs/charges is considered. Expenditures expensed and losses in the income statement do not offset one another, so the use of absolute values in the numerator is not required for income-statement triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure is not required if the aggregate income-statement amount of expenditures expensed and losses is less than $100,000 for the relevant fiscal year, or if the aggregate balance-sheet amount of capitalized costs and charges is less than $500,000 for the relevant fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De minimis thresholds are intended to reduce disproportionate burdens on smaller companies or companies near breakeven, and to mitigate concerns that a one percent threshold could produce immaterial disclosures for small registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate disclosure of recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must separately disclose any recoveries resulting from severe weather events and other natural conditions as part of the required contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement allows investors to see the net effect of severe weather events and other natural conditions on a registrant's financial statements even though the primary aggregated disclosure excludes recoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate disclosure of presentation line items
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are required to separately disclose where on the income statement and balance sheet (as applicable) the capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a disaggregation of financial-statement line items intended to enhance investor understanding of effects on financial position and performance and to facilitate year-on-year and cross-registrant comparisons. The Commission does not expect this to increase burden relative to the proposed metrics because it is based on existing line-item presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: transition-activity expenditures generally not required in financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require registrants to disclose costs and expenditures related to general transition activities in the financial statements at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted transition activities are often intertwined with ordinary business decisions and hard to attribute; requiring such disclosure in financial statements posed feasibility and forecasting issues. Some transition-related expenditures may still be required to be disclosed outside the financial statements under subpart 1500 (materiality-based disclosures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement for carbon offsets and RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose the aggregate amounts of (1) carbon offsets and RECs expensed, (2) carbon offsets and RECs capitalized, and (3) losses incurred on capitalized carbon offsets and RECs during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is not subject to the one percent threshold; it is required if carbon offsets or RECs have been used as a material component of a registrant's plan to achieve disclosed climate-related targets or goals. Registrants must also disclose beginning and ending balances of capitalized carbon offsets and RECs on the balance sheet and where such items are presented on financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and accounting basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses disclosed under the final rules are those already captured in a registrant's income statement or balance sheet and measured and reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP or IFRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using amounts as reported under existing accounting standards reduces burden compared to the proposed Financial Impact Metrics and ensures consistency with financial reporting. Registrants should consider relevant GAAP/IFRS presentation and disclosure practices when preparing the required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require disclosure of impacts to statement of cash flows
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require disclosure of the impacts to the statement of cash flows (the proposal's cash-flow impacts were not adopted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrowing reduces burden on registrants; the final rules focus on income-statement and balance-sheet aggregates instead of cash-flow line-item impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Item 1502 climate-risk identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require a registrant to disclose the impact of any climate-related risks identified pursuant to Item 1502(a) on the Expenditure Metrics or financial metrics included in the proposed rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the adopted disclosures are narrowly focused on capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses resulting from severe weather events and other natural conditions, linking them to Item 1502(a) climate-risk identification was not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual examples of expenditures to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules provide examples of expenditures that registrants may be required to disclose, such as amounts incurred to increase resilience of assets/operations, retire or shorten useful lives of impacted assets, relocate assets/operations at risk, reduce future impact of severe weather events, R&D of new technologies, purchase of assets/infrastructure to reduce GHGs or increase efficiency, purchase of energy credits/offsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate the types of discrete, attributable costs the Commission expects could be disclosed and emphasize that the final rules focus on expenditures incurred 'as a result of' severe weather events and other natural conditions rather than speculative or multi-motive transition investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAAP obligations and representational faithfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants remain obligated under GAAP to consider material impacts on financial statements; climate-related drivers do not alter financial reporting obligations, and additional disaggregation may be necessary to achieve a complete, neutral, and error-free representation per the FASB Conceptual Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should assess whether disaggregating material cash outflows or other expenditures on the face of primary statements or in notes (e.g., to show property, plant, and equipment purchases related to transition plans) is appropriate to provide complete information about entity cash flows and financial position.
